name: Niger Military Coup
description: Military junta led by General Tchiani overthrew President Bazoum in July 2023, expelled French forces and US military personnel, and invited Russian Africa Corps (formerly Wagner) to establish presence.
significance: Russia/Wagner gains Sahel foothold, French influence collapses across West Africa, uranium supply chain disrupted

name: Gabon Military Coup
description: Military officers overthrew the Bongo dynasty (56 years in power) minutes after disputed election results in August 2023. Transitional military government adopted non-aligned posture.
significance: French sphere of influence shrinks further in Central Africa, oil-rich Gulf of Guinea state becomes geopolitically unanchored

name: Myanmar Military Coup
description: Military (Tatmadaw) seized power in February 2021, detaining Aung San Suu Kyi. Junta deepened dependence on China for arms, diplomatic cover, and economic lifelines amid Western sanctions.
significance: BRI land corridor through Myanmar becomes junta-dependent, Kyaukpyu deep-sea port project accelerates under military rule, Indian Ocean access for China solidifies

name: Afghanistan Government Collapse
description: Taliban captured Kabul in August 2021 as US forces withdrew after 20 years. The Afghan government collapsed within days, stranding billions in military equipment.
significance: INSTC Afghan spur becomes a dead end, CPEC western extension blocked, China and Russia cautiously engage Taliban for mineral access and security guarantees

name: Sudan Civil War
description: Civil war erupted in April 2023 between SAF (General Burhan) and RSF (General Hemedti) after failed power-sharing. Preceded by 2019 revolution ousting Bashir and 2021 military coup dissolving civilian government.
significance: Red Sea coast becomes contested, Russian naval base at Port Sudan in limbo, East Africa corridor route destabilized, humanitarian catastrophe displaces millions

name: Fall of Assad / HTS Takeover
description: HTS-led opposition forces swept across Syria in late November 2024, capturing Aleppo, Homs, and Damascus by December 8. Assad fled to Moscow. Russia's Tartus naval base and Hmeimim airbase face uncertain future.
significance: Russia may lose its only Mediterranean naval facility, Iran's land bridge to Hezbollah severed, Eastern Mediterranean power balance shifts dramatically

name: Egyptian Military Takeover
description: General Sisi removed elected President Morsi in July 2013 amid mass protests. Military reasserted control over Suez Canal operations and restored Western-aligned foreign policy.
significance: Suez Canal security guaranteed under military rule, IMEC southern corridor anchor stabilized, $1.3B US annual military aid maintained

name: Sri Lanka Economic Collapse
description: Economic crisis forced President Rajapaksa to flee in July 2022 amid mass protests. Sovereign default on $51B debt. Hambantota Port (99-year Chinese lease) became symbol of debt-trap diplomacy debate.
significance: China's Indian Ocean 'string of pearls' strategy questioned, Hambantota renegotiation window opens under new government, India competes for Colombo port terminal

name: Imran Khan Ouster
description: PM Imran Khan removed via no-confidence vote in April 2022, later arrested and jailed. Political instability, military interference, and economic crisis cast CPEC's $62B investment into uncertainty.
significance: CPEC flagship projects stall, Gwadar port underutilized amid Balochistan insurgency, Pakistan oscillates between Chinese and Western alignment under IMF pressure

name: Milei Election — Argentine Pivot
description: Libertarian Javier Milei won presidency in November 2023, reversed predecessor's application to join BRICS, aligned firmly with US and Israel, and opened lithium/rare earth sectors to Western investment.
significance: Lithium triangle tilts Western, China loses potential BRICS ally in South America, critical mineral supply chain diversifies away from Chinese dominance

name: Fall of Gaddafi
description: NATO-backed uprising toppled Muammar Gaddafi in October 2011. Libya fractured into rival governments (Tripoli vs Tobruk), with Turkey, Russia, UAE, and Egypt backing opposing sides.
significance: Central Mediterranean becomes ungoverned corridor, Russian and Turkish military presence expands, oil exports weaponized by rival factions, migration route to Europe destabilized

name: Iraq Post-Invasion Political Shift
description: US invasion toppled Saddam Hussein in 2003. Subsequent elections empowered Shia-majority parties with deep Iranian ties. By 2005, Iran became the dominant external influence in Iraqi politics.
significance: Iraq Development Road corridor complicated by Iranian influence, Grand Faw Port project becomes Iran-adjacent chokepoint, IMEC overland route through Iraq politically uncertain

name: Arab Spring — Egypt Revolution
description: Mass protests in Tahrir Square toppled President Mubarak in February 2011 after 30 years of rule. Brief period of democratic uncertainty before Muslim Brotherhood's Morsi won 2012 election.
significance: Suez Canal transit security temporarily in question, insurance premiums spike for maritime traffic, demonstrated fragility of corridor-critical chokepoint governance

name: Burkina Faso Double Coup
description: Two military coups in January and September 2022. Captain Traore expelled French forces, invited Russian military instructors, and joined the Sahel alliance with Mali and Niger.
significance: Wagner/Africa Corps expands across Sahel belt, French military completely expelled from former colony, Russia builds contiguous influence zone in West Africa

name: Mali Military Coup
description: Colonel Goita seized power in May 2021 (second coup in nine months), expelled French and UN peacekeeping forces, and contracted Wagner Group for counterinsurgency operations.
significance: First domino in Sahel realignment cascade, France's Operation Barkhane collapses, Wagner establishes African operational model later replicated in Niger and Burkina Faso
